title: Grateful Dead Live at Hill Auditorium on 1971-12-15
lineage: FLAC/24 > Adobe Audition CC2015 > Samplitude Pro X4 Suite > FLAC/24
source: SBD > Master Reel > Pro Tools > FLAC/24

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1971 show featuring early Keith brilliance and a menacing Dark Star, captured in a crisp mix with keyboards front‑and‑center.
ai_review.review: Both reviewers rave about the inspired performance – tight playing, standout Dark Star, and lively banter – while noting that the recording sounds clear and balanced, reminiscent of the famed Europe ’72 tapes, with Keith's organ prominently in the mix. The show is praised as a transitional yet top‑notch entry in the Dead’s 1971 catalog.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong, energetic performance highlighted by Dark Star and excellent keyboard work combined with a clear, well‑balanced recording yields a high overall score; confidence is medium due to only two detailed reviews.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Keyboards sit high in the mix giving early Keith prominence; sound is crisp and balanced, reminiscent of Europe ’72 recordings; no dropouts or muddiness reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Smooth and tight throughout with inspired transitions; the band’s energy stays high, especially during the Dark Star segment.

band_member_comments.Keys: Early Keith is front‑and‑center – high in the mix, delivering great rock‑n‑roll organ and a distinct 'Keith‑ness' that defines the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann has clearly found his footing post‑Mickey, providing solid, confident drumming throughout.
